sanskrit: kṣatajokṣitasarvāṅgaḥ kṣaran sa rudhiraṃ vraṇaiḥ babhau rāmas tadā rājan merur dhātūn ivotsṛjan
english: His every limb drenched in blood, streaming gore from his wounds, Rāma shone then, O king, like Mount Meru pouring forth its mineral ores.

sanskrit: hemantānte 'śoka iva raktastabakamaṇḍitaḥ babhau rāmas tadā rājan kva cit kiṃśukasaṃnibhaḥ
english: Like an aśoka tree at winter's end adorned with clusters of red blossoms, Rāma shone then, O king, in places resembling a kiṃśuka in flower.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad dhanur ādāya rāmaḥ krodhasamanvitaḥ hemapuṅkhān suniśitāñ śarāṃs tān hi vavarṣa saḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, Rāma, filled with wrath, rained down upon me arrows keenly sharpened and fletched with gold.

sanskrit: te samāsādya māṃ raudrā bahudhā marmabhedinaḥ akampayan mahāvegāḥ sarpānalaviṣopamāḥ
english: Reaching me, those fearsome shafts, piercing my vital parts in many places, made me tremble — of mighty speed, like serpents, fire, and poison.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ samavaṣṭabhya punar ātmānam āhave śatasaṃkhyaiḥ śaraiḥ kruddhas tadā rāmam avākiram
english: Then I, steadying myself once more in the battle, in my wrath covered Rāma with arrows by the hundred.

sanskrit: sa tair agnyarkasaṃkāśaiḥ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ śitair abhyardito rāmo mandacetā ivābhavat
english: Sorely afflicted by those sharp arrows, blazing like fire and the sun and like venomous snakes, Rāma seemed to grow faint of mind.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ kṛpayāviṣṭo vinindyātmānam ātmanā dhig dhig ity abruvaṃ yuddhaṃ kṣatraṃ ca bharatarṣabha
english: Then, overcome with pity, reproaching myself within myself, I cried, 'Shame, shame upon this battle and upon the warrior's calling!' O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: asakṛc cābruvaṃ rājañ śokavegapariplutaḥ aho bata kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ mayedaṃ kṣatrakarmaṇā
english: And again and again I said, O king, swept away by the surge of grief: 'Alas, what an evil deed I have done through this warrior's office!'

sanskrit: gurur dvijātir dharmātmā yad evaṃ pīḍitaḥ śaraiḥ tato na prāharaṃ bhūyo jāmadagnyāya bhārata
english: 'My teacher, a brāhmaṇa, a man of righteous soul, is thus tormented by my arrows!' — and so I struck no longer at the son of Jamadagni, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: athāvatāpya pṛthivīṃ pūṣā divasasaṃkṣaye jagāmāstaṃ sahasrāṃśus tato yuddham upāramat
english: Then, having scorched the earth, the thousand-rayed Pūṣan, the sun, went down to his setting as the day waned, and with that the fighting ceased.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ātmanas tu tataḥ sūto hayānāṃ ca viśāṃ pate mama cāpanayām āsa śalyān kuśalasaṃmataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, O lord of peoples, my charioteer, esteemed for his skill, drew out the arrowheads from himself, from the horses, and from me.

sanskrit: snātopavṛttais turagair labdhatoyair avihvalaiḥ prabhāta udite sūrye tato yuddham avartata
english: When dawn broke and the sun had risen, with the horses bathed, rested, watered, and unwearied, the battle began again.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā māṃ tūrṇam āyāntaṃ daṃśitaṃ syandane sthitam akarod ratham atyarthaṃ rāmaḥ sajjaṃ pratāpavān
english: Seeing me come swiftly on, armored and standing in my chariot, the valiant Rāma made his own car fully ready for the fray.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ rāmam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā samarakāṅkṣiṇam dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ samutsṛjya sahasāvataraṃ rathāt
english: Then I, seeing Rāma advancing, eager for combat, set aside my excellent bow and at once stepped down from my chariot.

sanskrit: abhivādya tathaivāhaṃ ratham āruhya bhārata yuyutsur jāmadagnyasya pramukhe vītabhīḥ sthitaḥ
english: Having saluted him, I mounted my car again, O Bhārata, and, eager to fight and free of fear, took my stand before the son of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: tato māṃ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samavākirat ahaṃ ca śaravarṣeṇa varṣantaṃ samavākiram
english: Then he covered me with a great downpour of arrows, and I in turn covered him, as he rained his shafts, with a downpour of my own.

sanskrit: saṃkruddho jāmadagnyas tu punar eva patatriṇaḥ preṣayām āsa me rājan dīptāsyān uragān iva
english: But the son of Jamadagni, full of wrath, once more sent winged shafts against me, O king, like serpents with blazing mouths.

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ niśitair bhallaiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ acchidaṃ sahasā rājann antarikṣe punaḥ punaḥ
english: Those I cut down with sharp broad-headed arrows, by hundreds and by thousands, O king, cleaving them in the air again and again.

sanskrit: tatas tv astrāṇi divyāni jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān mayi pracodayām āsa tāny ahaṃ pratyaṣedhayam
english: Then the valiant son of Jamadagni loosed celestial weapons against me, and these I warded off.

sanskrit: astrair eva mahābāho cikīrṣann adhikāṃ kriyām tato divi mahān nādaḥ prādurāsīt samantataḥ
english: With weapon meeting weapon, O mighty-armed one, as he sought to gain the upper hand, a great roar arose in the heavens on every side.

sanskrit: tato 'ham astraṃ vāyavyaṃ jāmadagnye prayuktavān pratyājaghne ca tad rāmo guhyakāstreṇa bhārata
english: Then I employed the wind-weapon against the son of Jamadagni, but Rāma struck it back with the weapon of the Guhyakas, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato 'stram aham āgneyam anumantrya prayuktavān vāruṇenaiva rāmas tad vārayām āsa me vibhuḥ
english: Then I, with proper incantation, sent forth the fire-weapon, but the mighty Rāma turned mine aside with the weapon of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: evam astrāṇi divyāni rāmasyāham avārayam rāmaś ca mama tejasvī divyāstravid ariṃdamaḥ
english: Thus I warded off Rāma's celestial weapons, and Rāma too — blazing, knower of divine arms, subduer of foes — warded off mine.

sanskrit: tato māṃ savyato rājan rāmaḥ kurvan dvijottamaḥ urasy avidhyat saṃkruddho jāmadagnyo mahābalaḥ
english: Then, turning me to his left, O king, that foremost of brāhmaṇas, the mighty son of Jamadagni, in his fury pierced me in the chest.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ bharataśreṣṭha saṃnyaṣīdaṃ rathottame atha māṃ kaśmalāviṣṭaṃ sūtas tūrṇam apāvahat gorutaṃ bharataśreṣṭha rāmabāṇaprapīḍitam
english: Then I, O best of the Bhāratas, sank down upon my noble car, and the charioteer, seeing me overcome with faintness and sorely afflicted by Rāma's arrow, swiftly bore me away a krośa's distance, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato mām apayātaṃ vai bhṛśaṃ viddham acetasam rāmasyānucarā hṛṣṭāḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā pracukruśuḥ akṛtavraṇaprabhṛtayaḥ kāśikanyā ca bhārata
english: Then, seeing me borne off, grievously wounded and senseless, Rāma's followers — Akṛtavraṇa foremost among them, and the maiden of Kāśī — all rejoiced and raised a shout, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatas tu labdhasaṃjño 'haṃ jñātvā sūtam athābruvam yāhi sūta yato rāmaḥ sajjo 'haṃ gatavedanaḥ
english: Then, when I had regained my senses, I knew my situation and said to the charioteer: 'Drive on, charioteer, to where Rāma is; I am ready, my pain has passed.'

sanskrit: tato mām avahat sūto hayaiḥ paramaśobhitaiḥ nṛtyadbhir iva kauravya mārutapratimair gatau
english: Then the charioteer bore me on with steeds most splendid, as if dancing in their stride, O Kaurava, and equal to the wind in their swiftness.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ rāmam āsādya bāṇajālena kaurava avākiraṃ susaṃrabdhaḥ saṃrabdhaṃ vijigīṣayā
english: Then, reaching Rāma, O Kaurava, in great agitation I covered that agitated foe with a net of arrows, longing for victory.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evāsau rāmo bāṇān ajihmagān bāṇair evācchinat tūrṇam ekaikaṃ tribhir āhave
english: But as those straight-flying arrows came on, Rāma swiftly cut each single one with three arrows of his own in that battle.

sanskrit: tatas te mṛditāḥ sarve mama bāṇāḥ susaṃśitāḥ rāmabāṇair dvidhā chinnāḥ śataśo 'tha mahāhave
english: Then all those well-sharpened arrows of mine were shattered, cleft in two by Rāma's shafts, by the hundred in that great battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ punaḥ śaraṃ dīptaṃ suprabhaṃ kālasaṃmitam asṛjaṃ jāmadagnyāya rāmāyāhaṃ jighāṃsayā
english: Then again I loosed at the son of Jamadagni, at Rāma, a blazing, bright shaft equal to Death itself, seeking to slay him.

sanskrit: tena tv abhihato gāḍhaṃ bāṇacchedavaśaṃ gataḥ mumoha sahasā rāmo bhūmau ca nipapāta ha
english: Struck hard by it and brought under the power of that arrow's stroke, Rāma suddenly swooned and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ rāme bhūtalam āśrite jagad bhārata saṃvignaṃ yathārkapatane 'bhavat
english: Then, when Rāma had sunk to the earth, all the world cried out in dismay, and the whole creation grew troubled, O Bhārata, as if at the falling of the sun.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ susaṃvignāḥ sarva evābhidudruvuḥ tapodhanās te sahasā kāśyā ca bhṛgunandanam
english: Then, deeply alarmed, all those ascetics rich in penance, together with the maiden of Kāśī, rushed at once toward the delight of the Bhṛgus.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ saṃpariṣvajya śanair āśvāsayaṃs tadā pāṇibhir jalaśītaiś ca jayāśīrbhiś ca kaurava
english: Embracing him, they gently revived him then with hands cooled by water and with blessings for his victory, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vihvalo vākyaṃ rāma utthāya mābravīt tiṣṭha bhīṣma hato 'sīti bāṇaṃ saṃdhāya kārmuke
english: Then Rāma, still reeling, rose and spoke to me, fitting an arrow to his bow: 'Stand fast, Bhīṣma — you are as good as slain!'

sanskrit: sa mukto nyapatat tūrṇaṃ pārśve savye mahāhave yenāhaṃ bhṛśasaṃvigno vyāghūrṇita iva drumaḥ
english: Loosed, it fell swiftly upon my left side in that great battle, by which I was sorely shaken, reeling like a tree about to topple.

sanskrit: hatvā hayāṃs tato rājañ śīghrāstreṇa mahāhave avākiran māṃ viśrabdho bāṇais tair lomavāhibhiḥ
english: Then, having slain my horses in that great battle with his swift-weapon, O king, he confidently covered me with arrows fletched with feathers.

sanskrit: tato 'ham api śīghrāstraṃ samare 'prativāraṇam avāsṛjaṃ mahābāho te 'ntarādhiṣṭhitāḥ śarāḥ rāmasya mama caivāśu vyomāvṛtya samantataḥ
english: Then I too loosed in battle the swift-weapon that none could withstand, O mighty-armed one; and the arrows, Rāma's and mine alike, swiftly met and held the space between us, veiling the whole sky on every side.

sanskrit: na sma sūryaḥ pratapati śarajālasamāvṛtaḥ mātariśvāntare tasmin megharuddha ivānadat
english: The sun could not shine through, veiled by that web of arrows; and the wind, caught in that space between, roared as though pent in by clouds.

sanskrit: tato vāyoḥ prakampāc ca sūryasya ca marīcibhiḥ abhitāpāt svabhāvāc ca pāvakaḥ samajāyata
english: Then from the churning of the wind, from the rays of the sun, from the scorching heat, and from their own nature, the arrows kindled into fire.

sanskrit: te śarāḥ svasamutthena pradīptāś citrabhānunā bhūmau sarve tadā rājan bhasmabhūtāḥ prapedire
english: Those arrows, set ablaze by the fire risen from themselves, then all fell to the earth, O king, reduced to ashes.

sanskrit: tadā śatasahasrāṇi prayutāny arbudāni ca ayutāny atha kharvāṇi nikharvāṇi ca kaurava rāmaḥ śarāṇāṃ saṃkruddho mayi tūrṇam apātayat
english: Then by hundreds of thousands, by millions and tens of millions, by ten-thousands, by hundred-billions and thousand-billions, O Kaurava, Rāma in his wrath swiftly rained his arrows down upon me.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tān api raṇe śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ saṃchidya bhūmau nṛpate 'pātayaṃ pannagān iva
english: Then I too, with arrows like venomous serpents, cut those down in battle, O king, and brought them to earth like so many snakes.

sanskrit: evaṃ tad abhavad yuddhaṃ tadā bharatasattama saṃdhyākāle vyatīte tu vyapāyāt sa ca me guruḥ
english: Thus did that battle go, O best of the Bhāratas; and when the hour of twilight had passed, my teacher withdrew.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca samāgatasya rāmeṇa punar evātidāruṇam anyedyus tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ tadā bharatasattama
english: Bhīṣma said: When I had joined battle with Rāma once more, the next day there was again a fight most terrible and tumultuous, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato divyāstravic chūro divyāny astrāṇy anekaśaḥ ayojayata dharmātmā divase divase vibhuḥ
english: Then the hero, knower of celestial weapons, that righteous and mighty lord, deployed divine arms in great number, day after day.

sanskrit: tāny ahaṃ tatpratīghātair astrair astrāṇi bhārata vyadhamaṃ tumule yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā sudustyajān
english: Those weapons I scattered with counter-weapons, weapon against weapon, O Bhārata, in that tumultuous battle, having set aside this life so hard to give up.

sanskrit: astrair astreṣu bahudhā hateṣv atha ca bhārgavaḥ akrudhyata mahātejās tyaktaprāṇaḥ sa saṃyuge
english: When his weapons had been struck down again and again by mine, the Bhārgava of mighty splendor grew wrathful, having himself cast away all care for life in that combat.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaktiṃ prāhiṇod ghorarūpām; astrai ruddho jāmadagnyo mahātmā kālotsṛṣṭāṃ prajvalitām ivolkāṃ; saṃdīptāgrāṃ tejasāvṛtya lokān
english: Then the great-souled son of Jamadagni, his weapons blocked, hurled a spear of fearsome form, blazing like a meteor loosed by Time, its point aflame, wrapping the worlds in its glare.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ tām iṣubhir dīpyamānaiḥ; samāyāntīm antakālārkadīptām chittvā tridhā pātayām āsa bhūmau; tato vavau pavanaḥ puṇyagandhiḥ
english: Then, as it came on, blazing like the sun at the world's end, I cut it with flaming arrows into three pieces and brought it down to earth; whereupon a wind blew, fragrant and holy.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ chinnāyāṃ krodhadīpto 'tha rāmaḥ; śaktīr ghorāḥ prāhiṇod dvādaśānyāḥ tāsāṃ rūpaṃ bhārata nota śakyaṃ; tejasvitvāl lāghavāc caiva vaktum
english: When it was cut down, Rāma, ablaze with anger, hurled twelve more fearsome spears; their form, O Bhārata, could not be told, so dazzling were they and so swift.

sanskrit: kiṃ tv evāhaṃ vihvalaḥ saṃpradṛśya; digbhyaḥ sarvās tā maholkā ivāgneḥ nānārūpās tejasogreṇa dīptā; yathādityā dvādaśa lokasaṃkṣaye
english: Indeed I was bewildered to behold them, from every quarter, like great meteors of fire, of varied form, blazing with fierce splendor, like the twelve suns at the world's dissolution.

sanskrit: tato jālaṃ bāṇamayaṃ vivṛtya; saṃdṛśya bhittvā śarajālena rājan dvādaśeṣūn prāhiṇavaṃ raṇe 'haṃ; tataḥ śaktīr vyadhamaṃ ghorarūpāḥ
english: Then, spreading out a net made of arrows, sighting them and piercing them with that net of shafts, O king, I loosed twelve arrows in the battle, and so beat down those spears of fearsome form.

sanskrit: tato 'parā jāmadagnyo mahātmā; śaktīr ghorāḥ prākṣipad dhemadaṇḍāḥ vicitritāḥ kāñcanapaṭṭanaddhā; yathā maholkā jvalitās tathā tāḥ
english: Then the great-souled son of Jamadagni flung yet other fearsome spears with golden shafts, richly wrought and bound with bands of gold, blazing each like a great meteor.

sanskrit: tāś cāpy ugrāś carmaṇā vārayitvā; khaḍgenājau pātitā me narendra bāṇair divyair jāmadagnyasya saṃkhye; divyāṃś cāśvān abhyavarṣaṃ sasūtān
english: Those fierce spears too I warded off with my shield and struck down in battle with my sword, O lord of men; and with celestial arrows I rained upon the son of Jamadagni's divine horses and his charioteer.

sanskrit: nirmuktānāṃ pannagānāṃ sarūpā; dṛṣṭvā śaktīr hemacitrā nikṛttāḥ prāduścakre divyam astraṃ mahātmā; krodhāviṣṭo haihayeśapramāthī
english: Seeing his gold-wrought spears, like serpents new-sloughed of their skins, cut to pieces, the great-souled crusher of the Haihaya lord, seized by wrath, brought forth a celestial weapon.

sanskrit: tataḥ śreṇyaḥ śalabhānām ivogrāḥ; samāpetur viśikhānāṃ pradīptāḥ samācinoc cāpi bhṛśaṃ śarīraṃ; hayān sūtaṃ sarathaṃ caiva mahyam
english: Then ranks of blazing arrows came on, fierce as swarms of locusts, and densely covered my body, my horses, my charioteer, and my whole chariot.

sanskrit: rathaḥ śarair me nicitaḥ sarvato 'bhūt; tathā hayāḥ sārathiś caiva rājan yugaṃ ratheṣā ca tathaiva cakre; tathaivākṣaḥ śarakṛtto 'tha bhagnaḥ
english: My chariot was thickly studded with arrows on every side, and so too the horses and the charioteer, O king; the yoke, the pole, and likewise the wheels, and the axle as well, were cut by the arrows and broke.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin bāṇavarṣe vyatīte; śaraugheṇa pratyavarṣaṃ guruṃ tam sa vikṣato mārgaṇair brahmarāśir; dehād ajasraṃ mumuce bhūri raktam
english: Then, when that downpour of arrows had passed, I rained back a flood of shafts upon my teacher; and he, that mass of brahminic power, wounded by my missiles, poured ceaselessly much blood from his body.

sanskrit: yathā rāmo bāṇajālābhitaptas; tathaivāhaṃ subhṛśaṃ gāḍhaviddhaḥ tato yuddhaṃ vyaramac cāparāhṇe; bhānāv astaṃ prārthayāne mahīdhram
english: As Rāma was sorely tormented by my web of arrows, so was I most grievously and deeply wounded; then the battle ceased in the late afternoon, as the sun sought the mountain of its setting.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ prabhāte rājendra sūrye vimala udgate bhārgavasya mayā sārdhaṃ punar yuddham avartata
english: Bhīṣma said: Then at dawn, O lord of kings, when the sun had risen clear, the battle between the Bhārgava and me began once more.

sanskrit: tato bhrānte rathe tiṣṭhan rāmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi mayi śakra ivācale
english: Then, standing in his wheeling chariot, Rāma, best of warriors, rained showers of arrows upon me, as Śakra rains upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tena sūto mama suhṛc charavarṣeṇa tāḍitaḥ nipapāta rathopasthe mano mama viṣādayan
english: Struck by that downpour of arrows, my charioteer, who was my friend, fell to the floor of the chariot, casting my heart into grief.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūtaḥ sa me 'tyarthaṃ kaśmalaṃ prāviśan mahat pṛthivyāṃ ca śarāghātān nipapāta mumoha ca
english: Then that charioteer of mine, overcome by deep and great faintness, fell to the ground from the blows of the arrows and swooned away.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūto 'jahāt prāṇān rāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ muhūrtād iva rājendra māṃ ca bhīr āviśat tadā
english: Then the charioteer, sorely afflicted by Rāma's arrows, gave up his life within a moment, O lord of kings; and fear entered into me then.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūte hate rājan kṣipatas tasya me śarān pramattamanaso rāmaḥ prāhiṇon mṛtyusaṃmitān
english: Then, when my charioteer had been slain, O king, as I, distracted in mind, was loosing my arrows, Rāma sent against me shafts that were equal to Death.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūtavyasaninaṃ viplutaṃ māṃ sa bhārgavaḥ śareṇābhyahanad gāḍhaṃ vikṛṣya balavad dhanuḥ
english: Then, while I was distraught at the loss of my charioteer and in disarray, the Bhārgava, drawing his powerful bow, struck me hard with an arrow.

sanskrit: sa me jatrvantare rājan nipatya rudhirāśanaḥ mayaiva saha rājendra jagāma vasudhātalam
english: It fell, O king, between my collarbones — that blood-drinking shaft — and along with me, O lord of kings, it went down to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: matvā tu nihataṃ rāmas tato māṃ bharatarṣabha meghavad vyanadac coccair jahṛṣe ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Believing me slain, then, O bull of the Bhāratas, Rāma roared aloud like a thundercloud and rejoiced again and again.

sanskrit: tathā tu patite rājan mayi rāmo mudā yutaḥ udakrośan mahānādaṃ saha tair anuyāyibhiḥ
english: And when I had fallen thus, O king, Rāma, filled with joy, raised a great shout together with those his followers.

sanskrit: mama tatrābhavan ye tu kauravāḥ pārśvataḥ sthitāḥ āgatā ye ca yuddhaṃ taj janās tatra didṛkṣavaḥ ārtiṃ paramikāṃ jagmus te tadā mayi pātite
english: But the Kauravas who were there, standing at my side, and the people who had come, eager to behold that battle, fell into utmost anguish when I was struck down.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ pātito rājasiṃha; dvijān aṣṭau sūryahutāśanābhān te māṃ samantāt parivārya tasthuḥ; svabāhubhiḥ parigṛhyājimadhye
english: Then, fallen, O lion among kings, I beheld eight brāhmaṇas, radiant as the sun and fire; they stood surrounding me on every side and, in the midst of the battlefield, upheld me with their own arms.

sanskrit: rakṣyamāṇaś ca tair viprair nāhaṃ bhūmim upāspṛśam antarikṣe sthito hy asmi tair viprair bāndhavair iva svapann ivāntarikṣe ca jalabindubhir ukṣitaḥ
english: Guarded by those brāhmaṇas, I touched not the ground but remained held aloft in the air by those brāhmaṇas as by kinsmen, as if sleeping in mid-air, sprinkled with drops of water.

sanskrit: tatas te brāhmaṇā rājann abruvan parigṛhya mām mā bhair iti samaṃ sarve svasti te 'stv iti cāsakṛt
english: Then those brāhmaṇas, O king, holding me up, all said together, 'Fear not,' and again and again, 'May it be well with you.'

sanskrit: tatas teṣām ahaṃ vāgbhis tarpitaḥ sahasotthitaḥ mātaraṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhām apaśyaṃ ratham āsthitām
english: Then, refreshed by their words, I rose up at once and saw my mother, the best of rivers, standing in my chariot.

sanskrit: hayāś ca me saṃgṛhītās tayā vai; mahānadyā saṃyati kauravendra pādau jananyāḥ pratipūjya cāhaṃ; tathārṣṭiṣeṇaṃ ratham abhyaroham
english: And my horses had been held in check by her, the great river, in the midst of the battle, O lord of the Kurus; and I, having honored my mother's feet and likewise Ārṣṭiṣeṇa, mounted my chariot.

sanskrit: rarakṣa sā mama rathaṃ hayāṃś copaskarāṇi ca tām ahaṃ prāñjalir bhūtvā punar eva vyasarjayam
english: She had guarded my chariot, my horses, and all my gear; and I, with palms joined in reverence, then took my leave of her again.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ svayam udyamya hayāṃs tān vātaraṃhasaḥ ayudhyaṃ jāmadagnyena nivṛtte 'hani bhārata
english: Then I myself, taking up the reins of those wind-swift horses, fought on against the son of Jamadagni as the day waned, O Bhārata.
